harness_requirements.normative_sentence: JSON Schemas MUST use Draft 2020-12.
JSON Schemas MUST contain explicit `$schema` fields.
JSON Schemas MUST contain stable `$id` fields.
Governed artifact schemas MUST set `additionalProperties` to false.
JSON Schema `format` assertions MUST NOT be normative for ESRM v0.1 conformance.
Validators MUST NOT rely on library-specific `format` behavior for pass/fail decisions.
The artifact/domain registry MUST be closed.
The registry MUST map `proofrail.transition` to `PROOFRAIL:TRANSITION:V1`.
The registry MUST map `proofrail.signature` to `PROOFRAIL:SIGNATURE:V1`.
The registry MUST reject lowercase descriptive domain substitutes.
The rejection-stage and reason-code registry MUST be closed.
Raw artifact byte length MUST be no more than 1048576 bytes unless a later protocol revision changes the limit.
JSON nesting depth MUST be no more than 64.
Total parsed JSON node count MUST be no more than 100000.
Any object member count MUST be no more than 1024.
Any array length MUST be no more than 4096.
Any string byte length after UTF-8 encoding MUST be no more than 65536.
Requirement inventory MUST be generated from `ESRM_PROTOCOL_SECTIONS_22_40.md` and `ESRM_CONFORMANCE_HARNESS_REQUIREMENTS.md`.
Protocol requirements and harness requirements MUST have separate counts.

A requirement inventory MUST record requirement ID, source document, exact section, exact normative sentence, enforcement stage, planned positive vector IDs, planned negative vector IDs, implementation track, and coverage status.
A generated profile MUST NOT be the authority for its own coverage calculation.
A harness requirement MUST NOT be counted as protocol semantic coverage.
Until `.bin` files exist, the planning artifact MUST be named `binary-vector-plan.json`.
`binary-vector-plan.json` MUST state that no executable binary vectors are populated.
A future populated binary-vector manifest MUST enumerate actual `.bin` vector files.
`binary-vector-plan.json` MUST NOT claim to be a populated binary-vector manifest.
The future corpus generator MUST declare generator name, generator version, PRNG, seed format, and case-order rules.
The frozen generator name for this pack MUST be `proofrail-esrm-corpus-planner`.
The frozen generator version for this pack MUST be `0.1-repair2-plan-only`.
The frozen PRNG for future generated vector planning MUST be `HMAC-SHA256-DRBG` with seed encoded as lowercase hexadecimal bytes.
Case ordering MUST be lexicographic by `vector_id`.
Corpus planning MUST NOT depend on host time, process ID, local username, filesystem absolute paths, network state, or random device state after seed declaration.
Every validation or inventory-generation command referenced by a manifest or report MUST correspond to a committed script.

A clean checkout MUST provide one documented command that reproduces JSON parsing, schema meta-validation, instance validation, registry checks, requirement extraction, coverage calculation, and hash verification.
Validation tooling MUST use repository files and Python standard library only for this artifact phase.
Validation reports MUST NOT depend on uncommitted local packages.
The file-hash manifest MUST enumerate every governed file except itself.
harness_requirements.section: H8 - File Manifest and Release Root

harness_requirements.normative_sentence: The file-hash manifest exclusion MUST be explicit.
harness_requirements.section: H8 - File Manifest and Release Root

harness_requirements.normative_sentence: `file_hash_manifest_sha256` MUST be recorded separately from `release_root_record_sha256`.
harness_requirements.section: H8 - File Manifest and Release Root

harness_requirements.normative_sentence: The release-root record MUST record the immutable git commit when known.
harness_requirements.section: H8 - File Manifest and Release Root

harness_requirements.normative_sentence: A file-hash manifest MUST NOT claim to contain its own hash.
harness_requirements.section: H8 - File Manifest and Release Root

harness_requirements.normative_sentence: The file-manifest hash MUST NOT be mislabeled as the release-root record hash.
harness_requirements.section: H8 - File Manifest and Release Root

harness_requirements.normative_sentence: Future Rust and Go tracks MUST use independent parsing implementations.
Future Rust and Go tracks MUST use independent RFC 8785 canonicalization implementations.
Future Rust and Go tracks MUST use independent base64url implementations.
Future Rust and Go tracks MUST use independent Ed25519 verification implementations.
Future Rust and Go tracks MUST use independent JSON Schema validation implementations.
Future Rust and Go tracks MUST use independent SHA-256 or commitment implementations.
A Rust track MUST NOT call a Go validator for conformance decisions.
A Go track MUST NOT call a Rust validator for conformance decisions.
Rust implementation MUST NOT begin until the artifact pack passes independent file-by-file audit.
Go implementation MUST NOT begin until the artifact pack passes independent file-by-file audit.
Vector generation MUST NOT begin until the protocol and harness requirements are independently audited.
The artifact phase MUST NOT claim conformance.
The artifact phase MUST NOT implement lifecycle, dispatch, reconciliation, settlement, or recovery engines.
Repair 2 MUST record dispositions for `AUD-001` through `AUD-010`.
`AUD-001` MUST remain a failed-evidence finding against Repair 1.
Repair 2 MUST preserve Repair 1 commit `d405ca4dd5e0a766bbb1e9c1280742c51ebd3bd3` without rewriting it.

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: A signature verification result MUST mean only that a signature was produced by the private key corresponding to the resolved public key over the defined signature input.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 22 - Signature Does Not Confer Authority

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: A valid signature result MUST produce the state `ATTESTED` and MUST NOT produce the state `AUTHORIZED`.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 22 - Signature Does Not Confer Authority

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: Authorization MUST be derived from a separate authority input, policy input, or governance decision outside the signature envelope.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 22 - Signature Does Not Confer Authority

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: A verifier MUST NOT treat possession of a signing key as authority to perform, approve, dispatch, settle, reconcile, or recover an external effect.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 22 - Signature Does Not Confer Authority

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: A signature envelope MUST NOT embed a public key as the source of authority; key identity MUST resolve through a separate key-status or key-registry input.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 22 - Signature Does Not Confer Authority

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: A verifier MUST receive each artifact as an exact finite byte sequence before text decoding or JSON parsing.
A verifier MUST record diagnostic `raw_byte_length` outside the subject artifact.
A verifier MUST record diagnostic `raw_sha256` outside the subject artifact as SHA-256 over the exact raw byte sequence.
A verifier MUST NOT require, accept, or trust a subject artifact field that claims to contain the artifact's own raw byte hash.
A verifier MUST NOT normalize Unicode, line endings, or character encodings before raw-byte diagnostics are recorded.
JSON artifacts MUST be UTF-8 after raw-byte diagnostics are recorded.
JSON artifacts MUST contain exactly one top-level JSON object.
JSON object member names MUST be unique at every object depth.
JSON artifacts MUST NOT begin with a UTF-8 BOM.
JSON artifacts MUST NOT contain leading whitespace before the top-level object.
JSON artifacts MUST NOT contain trailing whitespace or trailing bytes after the top-level object.
JSON artifacts MUST NOT use comments, trailing commas, NaN, Infinity, or implementation-specific JSON extensions.
A verifier MUST apply strict intake checks before RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 25 - ESRM Strict Intake and Numeric Profile

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: JSON values MUST satisfy I-JSON constraints before canonicalization.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 25 - ESRM Strict Intake and Numeric Profile

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: Numeric values MUST be integers in the inclusive range 0 through 9007199254740991 unless a field schema forbids numbers entirely.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 25 - ESRM Strict Intake and Numeric Profile

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: Numeric-profile enforcement MUST apply recursively inside `critical_extensions` and `noncritical_extensions`.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 25 - ESRM Strict Intake and Numeric Profile

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: JSON numbers MUST NOT be negative, fractional, exponential, NaN, or Infinity.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 25 - ESRM Strict Intake and Numeric Profile

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: JSON strings MUST NOT contain unpaired surrogate code points.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 25 - ESRM Strict Intake and Numeric Profile

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: Canonicalization MUST use RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme after strict intake, I-JSON, schema, semantic, and numeric-profile checks.
Canonical bytes `B_x` MUST be defined as `UTF8(RFC8785Canonicalize(x))`.
A verifier MUST record diagnostic `canonical_bytes_hex` outside the subject artifact.
A verifier MUST record diagnostic `canonical_sha256` outside the subject artifact as SHA-256 over `B_x`.
A verifier MUST NOT require, accept, or trust a subject artifact field that claims to contain the artifact's own canonical hash.
A verifier MUST NOT substitute local member ordering, whitespace, or number rendering for RFC 8785 JCS.
Every governed artifact MUST declare `artifact_type` using the closed artifact-type registry.
A verifier MUST derive the registered domain from the closed registry using the artifact type.
Artifact-supplied values MUST never determine the registered domain.
Domain commitment `C_x` MUST be defined as `SHA256(ASCII(RegisteredDomain(artifact_type)) || 0x00 || B_x)`.
Domain commitment encoding MUST be exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
Registry values MUST NOT accept aliases, case variants, prefixes, suffixes, or lowercase descriptive substitutes.
A verifier MUST NOT replace the domain-separated commitment with an ordinary raw-byte or canonical-byte hash.
Every governed security artifact MUST require `artifact_type`.
Every governed security artifact MUST require `protocol_version`.
Every governed security artifact MUST require `crypto_suite`.
Every governed security artifact MUST require `critical_extensions`.
Every governed security artifact MUST require `noncritical_extensions`.
`critical_extensions` MUST be an array of extension entries.
`noncritical_extensions` MUST be an array of extension entries.
Governed artifact schemas MUST NOT make mandatory header fields optional.
Each extension entry MUST contain `extension_id` and `value`.
`extension_id` MUST match `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?::[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*)*:V[0-9]+$`.
An artifact MUST contain no more than 16 critical extension entries.
An artifact MUST contain no more than 64 noncritical extension entries.
Each serialized extension entry MUST be no more than 8192 bytes after JCS canonicalization.
A verifier MUST NOT ignore an unsupported critical extension.
Extension values MUST NOT contain values that violate the recursive numeric profile.
The ESRM v0.1 crypto suite MUST be `PR-ESRM-JCS-SHA256-ED25519-v1`.
Hashing MUST use SHA-256.
Signature verification MUST use pure Ed25519 per RFC 8032.
Signature encoding MUST be unpadded base64url that decodes to exactly 64 bytes.
Public-key encoding in key registries MUST be unpadded base64url that decodes to exactly 32 raw Ed25519 public-key bytes.
Verifiers MUST reject invalid Ed25519 point encodings and noncanonical signature scalar values.
Verifiers MUST NOT accept permissive Base64 decoding, padding, whitespace, mixed alphabets, or alternative alphabets for ESRM signature and public-key encodings.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `artifact_type` equal to `proofrail.transition`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `protocol_version`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `crypto_suite`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `transition_id`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `nonce`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `epoch`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `pre_state`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `rules`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `authority`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `transition`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `execution`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `settlement`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `critical_extensions`.
A `proofrail.transition` artifact MUST contain `noncritical_extensions`.
A transition schema MUST NOT substitute `operation_label`, `input_commitments`, or `output_commitments` for the supplied canonical transition package.
A transition artifact MUST NOT contain self-referential `raw_sha256` or `canonical_sha256` fields.

Unsigned signature envelope `E_tau` MUST contain exactly `artifact_type`, `protocol_version`, `crypto_suite`, `signed_artifact_type`, `signed_artifact_domain`, `signed_commitment`, `signer_id`, `key_id`, `critical_extensions`, and `noncritical_extensions`.
The transmitted `proofrail.signature` object MUST add exactly the `signature` field to `E_tau`.
The signature input MUST be `ASCII("PROOFRAIL:SIGNATURE:V1") || 0x00 || UTF8(JCS(E_tau))`.
`signed_artifact_domain` MUST equal the closed registry domain for `signed_artifact_type`.
`signed_commitment` MUST be the domain-separated commitment of the signed artifact.
A signature envelope MUST NOT embed the public key.
A signature envelope MUST NOT omit `signer_id`, `key_id`, `signed_artifact_type`, or `signed_artifact_domain`.
`key_id` MUST resolve through a separate key-registry or key-status input.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 33 - Key Registry and Key Status

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: The key-registry public key representation MUST be exactly 32 raw Ed25519 bytes encoded as unpadded base64url.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 33 - Key Registry and Key Status

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: Signature verification MUST fail closed when `key_id` is unknown, revoked, malformed, or incompatible with the declared crypto suite.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 33 - Key Registry and Key Status

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: A verifier MUST NOT use a public key supplied inside the signature envelope as the trust root.
protocol_requirements.section: Section 33 - Key Registry and Key Status

protocol_requirements.normative_sentence: A valid signature over a valid envelope MUST produce `ATTESTED` only.
Authority evaluation MUST consume separate authority material and MUST be distinguishable from signature verification.
A verifier MUST NOT conflate `ATTESTED` with authorization to execute external effects.
Reconciliation inputs and outputs MUST be content-addressed by domain-separated commitments.
Reconciliation rules MUST be append-only over prior commitments.
Reconciliation MUST NOT mutate or replace prior committed artifacts.
Consumption of authority or settlement capacity MUST be represented as an irreversible transition over committed inputs.
A consumed authority unit MUST NOT be reused by another transition.
External effects MUST be outside raw canonicalization conformance unless represented as committed observations.
A conformance lab MUST distinguish artifact verification from dispatch or execution.
Passing artifact verification MUST NOT imply that an external effect occurred or was authorized.
A conformance result MUST include `raw_byte_length`, `raw_sha256`, `canonical_bytes_hex`, `canonical_sha256`, and `domain_commitment` as verifier observations when applicable.
A conformance result MUST identify the rejection stage and reason code for rejected artifacts.
A conformance result MUST NOT be embedded in the subject artifact whose bytes it measures.
A populated binary-vector manifest MUST enumerate actual `.bin` files.
Each binary vector entry MUST contain `vector_id`.
Each binary vector entry MUST contain `relative_path`.
Each binary vector entry MUST contain `raw_byte_length`.
Each binary vector entry MUST contain `raw_sha256`.
Each binary vector entry MUST contain `expected_status`.
Accepted vectors MUST contain `expected_canonical_bytes_hex`, `expected_canonical_sha256`, `expected_domain_commitment`, and `expected_signature_result`.
Rejected vectors MUST contain `expected_rejection_stage` and `expected_reason_code`.
A requirement-planning inventory MUST NOT be called a populated binary-vector manifest.
Rejection precedence MUST be deterministic.
Rejection stages MUST be selected from the closed rejection-stage registry.
Reason codes MUST be selected from the closed reason-code registry.
Earlier rejection stages MUST take precedence over later stages when multiple failures are present.
A verifier MUST NOT report implementation-specific or nondeterministic rejection reasons for ESRM-governed vectors.
Any supplied Section 22-40 sentence not present in this repository document MUST remain an unresolved audit gap until inserted verbatim or adjudicated by an independent protocol owner.
Implementations MUST NOT begin from this document until independent audit confirms that the supplied Sections 22-40 semantics are preserved.
